slides.heading: Strings as Data
slides.body: Strings as Data is part of Variables and Primitive Data Types. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Strings as Data
slides.body: A string stores text data. Names, labels, addresses, and messages are usually represented as strings.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A string is like a word written on a sign. The quotation marks are the frame that tells Python the content is text.

annotations.note: This line stores or updates a value using a variable.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use clear variable names and match the data type to the kind of value you need to store.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Store your favorite subject as a string and print it.
slides.hint: Text must be placed inside quotation marks.

quiz.prompt_text: In Python, how do you correctly store text as a string?
quiz.explanation: Perfect! Strings must be wrapped in matching quotation marks on both sides. course = "Python" is the correct syntax.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to store a course name as a string and print it.

lines: # Store a course name as a string

quiz.explanation: The comment explains the goal first, then the string is stored in the variable, and finally print() displays the text value.

quiz.prompt_text: Store your favorite subject as a string in a variable named subject and print it.

content.hint: Text must be placed inside quotation marks. Then use print(subject).

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: Write subject = "Math" (or any subject) in quotes, then print(subject). Quotation marks tell Python the value is text, not a variable name.
